## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing integrate, decide, respawn, and render into a single register-only pass with no intermediate storage can approach the streaming ceiling by eliminating intermediate traffic.

## Layout & approach
The AoS Particle layout carries 68 B/p; the fused loop touches 48 (age+color+pos+seed+vel) — 70% hot, 20 bytes dead filler per line. No intermediate storage is allocated; the death verdict stays in registers and the render is a scatter reduction into the framebuffer. The particle stream is sequential (68-byte stride, prefetch-friendly), but the render writes scattered bytes at computed (x,y) offsets — random-address read-modify-writes that defeat prefetch and coalescing.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p is strikingly flat: 22.98 at N=320 (L1d) vs 22.47 at N=10M (DRAM) for q=0.01 — no knee at the L1d spill (N≈481), L2 spill (N≈7710), or L3 spill (N≈246723). A mild rise peaks near the L2/L3 boundary (N=7700–12000) but recovers in DRAM. This flatness refutes the cache premise of the hypothesis: eliminating intermediate traffic does not help because the kernel is scatter-bound, not streaming-bound — if bandwidth were the limiter, cost would climb at each spill.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth holds at 2.0–3.0 GB/s — 16–24% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — against a memory floor of 5.359 ns/p. The algo runs 4–6× above the floor; backend_stall dominates at 58.9–63.9%, compute at 24–25%, branch_flush at 12–15%. vs baseline: roughly parity (1.038× at q=0.01/N=320, 0.879× at N=10M). vs the autovec winner: 3.1–3.4× slower at q=0.01, narrowing to 1.74–1.96× at q=0.5 as branch_flush rises (11.8%→15.2%) and erodes the winner's SIMD advantage.

## Assembly
The codegen is overwhelmingly scalar: 15 vector instructions in 343, only 6 vector FP (`vmulps`, `vaddps`) against 20 scalar (`vmulss`, `vaddss`). Integration loads via `vmovups`/`vmovsd` but computes component-wise. The render scatter dominates: 23 byte-granular read-modify-write sequences, each `movzx` load, `add`, `cmp` 0xff, `cmovae` clamp, `mov BYTE PTR` store — dependent chains on random framebuffer addresses. The 12 `cmovae` implement select-based clamping; 32 conditional branches per iteration drive the 12–15% branch_flush.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter cannot stream. At q=0.01 the algo achieves 2.96 GB/s (23% of ceiling), 4.3× above the memory floor, with 63.9% backend stalls from 23 byte-granular read-modify-writes per particle. It matches naive scalar (0.88–1.05× baseline) but is 2.1–3.4× slower than the autovec winner at q=0.01, narrowing to 1.74–1.96× at q=0.5 where branch_flush equalizes both. The byte-granular scatter is the binding constraint.
